Alex — great to chat, thanks for the clear agenda. Below is a focused devkit quickstart + short checklist to get Lumina engineers running locally and to prepare for the tech workshop. I kept the steps minimal so your devs can hit a working loop in ~30–60 minutes.

1) Quickstart repos & links
- Single repo (examples): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/tree/main/lumina-quickstart
- Dev guide (one-pager): https://drive.redwood.ai/s/1a2b3c/quickstart-guide (attached PDF)

2) Local prerequisites
- Node 20.x (or latest LTS) and Python 3.11+
- Docker (optional but recommended for consistent env)
- Yarn or npm, pip and virtualenv

3) Minimal commands (Python)
- git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples.git
- cd sdk-examples/lumina-quickstart/python
- python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
- pip install -r requirements.txt
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=pk_dev_yoursample
- REDWOOD_API_URL=https://api.redwood.ai python app.py --mode local

4) Minimal commands (TypeScript)
- cd sdk-examples/lumina-quickstart/typescript
- yarn install
- cp .env.example .env && edit REDWOOD_API_KEY
- yarn dev  # starts local server + UI

5) Local testing notes
- Sample dataset: 1000 synthetic docs included under /data/sample_docs.json (run ./tools/index_sample.sh)
- Embedding batch size: start with 512 concurrent docs per batch, adjust based on local GPU/CPU memory. For production indexing we recommend Redwood Bulk Indexer (we can demo).

6) Auth patterns 
- Sandbox recommendation: API key + short-lived session tokens. We include a helper script (tools/ephemeral_token.py) that exchanges a long-lived service key for 1-hour tokens. In prod use your KMS to rotate the long-lived key.
- Example env vars: REDWOOD_API_KEY=pk_dev_xxx, REDWOOD_SESSION_TTL=3600

7) Routing / canary config (example)
- Attach a sample routing YAML under examples/routing/canary.yml. Key points: route by path=patient-search -> prefer model=redwood-embedding-2 for embeddings, fallback to redwood-embedding-2q (quant) when region=eu or cost-tier=low. Canary sample: 10% traffic -> quantized model.

8) Structured output & tool calling
- Types: the TS sample shows a tool definition for /vet with a JSON schema and a call pattern using the SDK tool.call({name, inputSchema, input}). The Python sample includes the equivalent call and a small JSON schema validator stub.

9) Embeddings & reranker suggestion
- Start: model=redwood-embed-2 (good balance of cost/quality).
- Rerank: use a two-stage scoring: cheap embed dot-product to shortlist (k=100), then rerank with a small tuned ranking model (redwood-rerank-1). We include a sample reranker scoring script under examples/rerank/score.py.

10) Next steps / workshop slots
- Proposed tech workshop: Tue 2028-04-30 10:00–11:30 PT (I can bring Karthik for the runtime deep-dive and Ben for commercial questions). Please confirm or propose alternate slots.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (one-pager), lumina-integration-checklist.xlsx

If this looks good I’ll share a curated checklist for your SRE to run tomorrow and we’ll prep the demo data.

Best,
